A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research, renamed from PrivacyPAD to Privacy-R1. The complete main text, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A–B are readable and support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original PUPA and Med-PCD evaluations, learning curves, ablations, and sensitivity analyses, plus a 240-instance human validation study in Appendix B.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical results, including the benchmark evaluations and Appendix B's human validation outcomes.

M1.justification: Sections 4.1–4.4 retain sentence chunking, frozen MiniLM embeddings, Transformer routing, the quadratic leakage penalty, supervised warm-up, and PPO. The new name and framework diagram describe the existing procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions use general-domain PUPA, including its New/TNB subsets, and medical Med-PCD. The additional application domains mentioned in v2's introduction are background examples, not added training or evaluation coverage.

E2.justification: Table 3 retains PAPILLON, Always-Local, Heuristic Router (SFT-only), and unredacted/redacted GPT-4o-mini controls. The stateless-router and linear-penalty ablation comparators also remain unchanged.

E3.justification: The Med-PCD 816/204 training/test split, remote model, five local-model configurations, evaluation metrics, and training budgets are unchanged. Appendix B retains the same 240-instance annotation protocol. No revised experimental procedure is reported.

E4.justification: Sections 6.2–6.4 retain the learning-dynamics analysis, stateful-versus-stateless ablation, linear-versus-quadratic penalty comparison, and lambda sensitivity sweep. The illustrative case in Figure 1 and validation analysis in Appendix B are also retained.

E5.justification: Both versions retain the same three-rater agreement analysis using Fleiss' kappa and identical learning-curve displays. v2 adds no seed counts, repeated-run information, uncertainty-estimation procedures, or significance tests.

E6.justification: Matched entries in Tables 1–6 and the learning curves are unchanged. For example, the proposed method's Llama-3.1-8B Med-PCD quality/leakage remains 89.5%/5.1%. Appendix B retains the 98.8% pass rate and kappa of 0.89.

T1.justification: The quality and leakage definitions, policy equations, binary TaskGain definition, quadratic reward, and PPO objectives are retained. The new framework diagram restates existing mathematics; no new formal assumption, derivation, theorem, or proof appears.

C1.justification: Despite the revised title, the abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same central contributions: learned chunk routing, the Med-PCD benchmark, and improved privacy–utility performance over static approaches.

C2.justification: The explanations concerning contextual routing, catastrophic leakage, local-model strength, and lambda remain unchanged. Both versions retain the single-turn and binary-routing limitations and explicitly state that the method provides no formal privacy guarantee.

D1.justification: The abstract replaces a promise to release code and data upon acceptance with a dataset repository link, dropping the explicit code-release promise. Section 5.3 removes the GPU count from '2 NVIDIA H200 GPUs'. Other implementation details and Appendix A's prompt are retained.

R1.justification: v2 adds contextual citations concerning synthetic data, education, legal applications, and memory/agent systems, plus Dong et al. (2026b) in related work. The central positioning against static rewriting and the claimed novelty of RL-based routing remain unchanged.

P1.justification: The title and framework name change, the affiliation changes from Monash University to University College London, and the introduction's opening is expanded. Section order and most prose, including both appendices, remain unchanged.

P2.justification: v2 adds an overview of routing and training as Figure 2 and relabels/reformats Figure 1. The unchanged learning curves become Figure 3, and existing tables shift with page reflow while retaining their structure and content.

improvement.justification: The new framework diagram provides an integrated overview of routing and two-stage training, while the abstract supplies a concrete dataset access location. These offer modest clarity and access benefits, tempered by removal of the exact GPU count and code-release promise. The scientific evidence and conclusions remain unchanged.
